canonical_inventory.resolution: The matrix method forbids removing rows, so all 25 canonical rows A1..F3 are dispositioned. The request-count mismatch is recorded, not silently normalized.

claim_limit: This receipt is a cited disposition of the complete canonical cross-invariant matrix. It changes no product byte and claims no new fixture, hardware, restage, promotion or acceptance result. OPEN dispositions are proposals for line-by-line Class-C review, not authorization to implement them.

method.OPEN: neither; one proposed fixture/addendum/benign disposition is mandatory
method.PROVEN: receipt or passed gate directly covers the crossing

citations.quote: "gc_after_each_new_heap_allocation": 2; canonical C2D root_values; writebacks 0
publish c2_pending_roots before any later allocation
The seam validates the canonical root range and publishes c2_pending_roots.

rows.finding: Allocation-triggered collection is permitted while the append transaction is open.  The canonical root high-water is published before each later allocation, and the direct append stress fixture collected after each of two new heap values without losing the transaction or exposing an uncommitted header.
rows.proof_boundary: Direct host stress plus the current product source seam prove root visibility and transaction survival; this is not a target timing claim.

citations.quote: committed low root prefix plus root intervals of all active transient records
watermark is raised first, before records and Attic bytes are wiped
19/19 cases; exact meet accepted; +1 rejected; 96 blockreads per collection
2 collections, 192 blockreads, 96 per collection

rows.finding: Active high-edge roots use the sole C2D root plane.  A transient transaction raises the scan bound to the complete root capacity; the collector reads it in 32-byte blocks.  Watermark raise precedes wipe, so an abort makes handles unreachable before reclamation.
rows.proof_boundary: The root-surface crossing and block transport are directly covered; the 82-frame GC envelope remains informative and limit-free.

citations.quote: The collector is non-moving and performs no writeback.
Execution uses Chip-RAM planes and removes runtime Attic reads.
hot entry uses Bank 2; native refill uses Bank 3; forbidden edges empty

rows.finding: The collector marks Lisp objects but does not relocate object cells. C2-lite code windows, Bank-2 code, Bank-3 native slices and C2D directory state are raw, fixed external planes outside the heap.
rows.structural_exclusion: A non-moving mark/sweep collector has no operation that can move or rewrite raw code/window/C2D storage; those planes are not collected objects.

citations.quote: watermark is published last inside the existing non-GC-interruptible publication seam
header/watermark after the plan; export cells next; READY last
The committed publication loop validates rows and writes symbol cells without allocation.

rows.finding: The publication store is a contracted non-GC-interruptible seam. All allocating resolution work and root publication precede it; the header/watermark commit and export-cell stores allocate nothing.
rows.structural_exclusion: Natural GC can occur during earlier resolution, but the contracted publication seam itself contains no allocation or collector entry.

citations.quote: central abort landing validates and restores C2J; journal cleared last
48 cases including longjmp-depth-1..4 and every append/unpublish cutpoint
c2_product_abort_cleanup executes before longjmp

rows.finding: The central abort landing restores the generation-bound C2J before longjmp.  Persistent and transient cutpoints at depths one through four restore exact prior state and retain committed descendants.
rows.proof_boundary: The contract model is bound to the implemented single abort landing.

citations.quote: 18/18 RUN/STOP cutpoints; one central cleanup before longjmp
C2D before/after SHA identical; directory growth 0; REPL survived

rows.finding: RUN/STOP and ordinary errors use the same abort landing and C2J driver.  The current product gate covers 18 break cutpoints, and Link 57 hardware observed byte-identical C2D before/after break.
rows.proof_boundary: Fresh structural product proof and same-identity hardware proof both cover the crossing.

disposition.proposed_action: Extend the abort-continuity contract to all product DMA seams: no longjmp/poll inside a submitted transport; a queued break is delivered exactly once at the first safe evaluator boundary. Add cutpoint fixtures before submit, during convergence and after proof.

rows.finding: Current delivery is polling-based and the transport/convergence closures do not intentionally call lisp_poll, but no contract states the defer-until-safe rule and no fixture injects RUN/STOP at the DMA setup/completion cutpoints.

citations.quote: The final C2D image has no source locator and no post-READY consumer may interpret it.
After READY no VM, GC, RUN/STOP, Freezer-return or resumable error path may read Attic.
724 hot relocations examined; forbidden control/data edges empty

rows.finding: C2-lite has no post-READY source locator and forbids all execution-time Attic reads.  Newer or stale Session-Attic bytes cannot be reached by an old directory; only unpublished cold staging may read them.
rows.structural_exclusion: The asymmetric content may physically exist, but no published directory edge can name or consume it in C2-lite.

rows.proof_boundary: Ordering and both disjoint closures are fresh gates on the Link 57 identity.

citations.quote: code/modifiers captured from one queue head and dequeued exactly once

The consumer reads the ordinary D60A/D619 queue head; no separate full-queue break latch is visible.

disposition.closure_condition: Queue-full break fixture and source-identity gate pass; no second handwritten key map is introduced.
disposition.proposed_action: Choose and contract a gapless RUN/STOP source when the typed queue is full (independent matrix latch or proved hardware queue rule), then fill the queue, press RUN/STOP and require exactly one abort with ordinary tuple ordering preserved.

rows.finding: Atomic one-head/one-dequeue capture is proven, and handoff continuity requires a pending abort latch.  Neither evidence defines the MEGA65 queue-full behavior nor proves that a newly pressed RUN/STOP cannot be lost behind a full ordinary key queue.

citations.quote: hot reads consume only the identity- and generation-bound published plane

rows.finding: The hot materializer is stateless, every vm_run entry refills its code window, and restage clears READY/generation before a new family can publish.  No cache survives across the lifecycle boundary.
rows.structural_exclusion: There is no generation-persistent hot state to invalidate.

citations.quote: Generation wrap requires cold boot. Hot restage remains forbidden.

rows.finding: Hot restage is forbidden.  The only product restage boundary is a cold boot that first makes READY false and resets the resident generation to zero; no running-session operation increments a u16 generation toward wrap.
rows.structural_exclusion: No in-product increment exists; cold boot reconstructs from zero. A future hot-restart feature would reopen this row.
